statement: A degeneration to five lines produces the lower bound 12·2⁵+5·3·2·2⁴+10·4·2³+1=1185 for conics with five tangencies to a plane quintic.

answer.text: The paper gives the historical lower bound 1185 for the complex number of five-contact conics.

source.location: Final displayed sum and paragraph, printed page 19; editor’s note, pages 19–20

notes:
Source-asserted classical geometric lower bound; not independently reconstructed as a modern deformation proof in this audit. The author and editor explicitly decline an exactness assertion. It does not prove 1185 real conics. The editor corrects a coefficient in an earlier de Jonquières formula, so 1135 is not retained as a verified count.

Imported from the 2026-10-26 catalogue record R_195eb1fa4d7989e0; the source claim has not been newly rechecked against the paper for this beta import.
scope: Nonsingular plane conics tangent at five distinct points to one general smooth plane quintic.
